breakfast.name: Ladob Salé (Savory Breadfruit)
instructions: Boil breadfruit in coconut milk
Add salted fish, onion, ginger, garlic, chili
Simmer until thick
breakfast.description: Savory breadfruit in coconut milk with fish.

breakfast.name: Rougaille Oeuf (Egg Rougaille)
instructions: Make tomato sauce with onion, garlic, ginger, thyme
Crack eggs into sauce
Cook until set
breakfast.description: Eggs in spicy Creole tomato sauce.

breakfast.name: Ladob (Sweet Ripe Plantain)
instructions: Ladob is the Seychellois sweet dish of ripe plantain cooked in coconut milk
The ripe plantain: very yellow, almost black -- maximum sweetness
Cooked in sweetened coconut milk with warm spices
Can be breakfast or dessert -- sweet but substantial
The Seychellois Creole cuisine blends African, French, Indian, and Chinese influences
breakfast.description: Seychellois sweet plantain in coconut milk -- very ripe plantains simmered in sweetened coconut milk with cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla. Can be breakfast or dessert. Seychellois Creole cuisine blends African, French, Indian, and Chinese traditions.

breakfast.name: French Bread with Butter and Jam
ingredients: French baguette (baked daily in Seychelles -- French colonial heritage)
Local jam: papaya, mango, or guava
instructions: French baguette is baked fresh daily throughout Seychelles
A legacy of French colonization (1742-1810)
Even after British colonization and independence, the French bread tradition persists
Local tropical jams: papaya, mango, guava -- made from island fruit
The combination of French technique and tropical fruit is distinctly Seychellois
breakfast.description: Seychellois French baguette with tropical jam -- fresh daily baguette (French colonial legacy from 1742-1810) with butter and local papaya, mango, or guava jam. Even after British colonization, the French bread tradition persisted. French technique, tropical flavors.

lunch.name: Kat-Kat Banane (Fish and Banana Curry)
instructions: Cook fish in coconut curry
Boil green bananas separately
Add bananas to curry
Simmer until thick
lunch.description: Fish curry with green bananas in coconut milk.

lunch.name: Octopus Curry Seychellois
instructions: Tenderize octopus, dice
Sauté aromatics with curry and masala
Add coconut milk and tomatoes
Add octopus, simmer 25 min
lunch.description: Tender octopus in rich coconut curry.

lunch.name: Rougaille de Saucisses (Sausage Creole Sauce)
ingredients: Rougaille sauce: tomatoes, onion, garlic, ginger, chilli, thyme
instructions: Rougaille is the Seychellois Creole tomato sauce -- the base sauce of the cuisine
From the Reunionnais Creole tradition: rougail/rougaille (tomato-chilli sauce)
The sauce: tomatoes, onion, garlic, ginger, and chilli
Can be made with fish, meat, sausages, or prawns
Sausage rougaille: smoked sausages braised in the rougaille sauce
Served with rice -- the standard accompaniment
lunch.description: Seychellois smoked sausage in Creole tomato sauce -- sausages braised in rougaille (tomatoes, onion, garlic, ginger, and chilli). Rougaille is the mother sauce of Seychellois Creole cooking, shared with Reunion island. Served with white rice.

lunch.name: Grilled Tuna Steak
instructions: Seychelles sits in the Indian Ocean -- tuna is caught in local waters
The yellowfin tuna: the most prized tuna species
Grilled fresh tuna steak: the simplest and best preparation
Marinated briefly with garlic, lemon, and chilli
Seared quickly on high heat -- the inside stays rare to medium
Freshness is everything with tuna
lunch.description: Seychellois grilled yellowfin tuna -- fresh tuna steak from Indian Ocean waters, marinated with garlic, lemon, and chilli, seared on high heat to rare-to-medium. The Seychelles Indian Ocean location provides exceptional fresh tuna.

lunch.name: Satini Requiem (Shark Chutney)
instructions: Satini requiem is the Seychellois shark chutney -- a specialty
Requiem: the name for shark in Seychellois Creole
The shark meat is cooked (smoked or boiled) then flaked
Mixed with bilimbi (a very sour fruit related to carambola) or lime
The sourness and the shredded shark: the distinctive combination
Eaten as a condiment alongside the main meal
lunch.description: Seychellois shark chutney -- cooked, flaked shark meat (requiem: the Creole word for shark) mixed with bilimbi (very sour fruit) or lime juice, onion, and chilli. Eaten as a condiment alongside the main dish. A Seychellois specialty.

dinner.name: Grilled Fish with Satini
ingredients: Satini: green papaya, chili, lime, onion
instructions: Grate green papaya, mix with chili, lime, onion for satini
Season fish, grill until flaky
Serve with satini and rice
dinner.description: Grilled fish with green papaya chutney.

dinner.name: Bat Curry
instructions: Clean and joint bats
Make curry with aromatics
Add bats and coconut milk
Simmer 40 min

dinner.name: Pwason Griye (Grilled Fish Creole)
instructions: Grilled whole fish with rougaille sauce is the Seychellois fish dinner
The fish is scored and marinated
Grilled over coals
Served with rougaille sauce poured over or alongside
The combination of grilled fish and tomato-chilli rougaille
dinner.description: Seychellois grilled whole fish -- red snapper or grouper scored, marinated with garlic and lime, grilled over coals, served with rougaille sauce (Creole tomato-chilli). The standard Seychellois fish dinner.

dinner.name: Cari Zourit (Octopus Curry)
instructions: Octopus curry is a Seychellois specialty -- Indian Ocean octopus
The octopus must be tenderized first -- boiled or beaten
Braised in a coconut milk curry
The Indian influence in the curry spices: the Seychellois Indian community (from Bombay)
The result: tender octopus in an aromatic coconut curry
dinner.description: Seychellois octopus curry -- Indian Ocean octopus tenderized then braised in coconut milk with curry powder, ginger, and turmeric. The Indian community (from Bombay, arriving in the 19th century) introduced curry spices to Seychellois cooking.

dinner.name: Riz Creole (Creole Rice)
instructions: Riz Creole is the Seychellois rice preparation -- not plain white, not completely coconut
A small amount of coconut milk is added to the cooking water
The rice absorbs a gentle coconut fragrance
The grains are separate -- not sticky
Served alongside every Seychellois meal
dinner.description: Seychellois Creole rice -- long-grain rice cooked with a small amount of coconut milk for gentle coconut fragrance, grain-separate, fluffy. The standard accompaniment to every Seychellois meal.

snacks.name: Gato Piman (Chili Cakes)
instructions: Grind peas coarsely
Mix with chili, onion, cumin
Fry spoonfuls until golden
snacks.description: Spicy split pea fritters — Seychelles' favorite snack.

snacks.name: Kari Bred (Leaf Curry Fritters)
ingredients: Leafy greens (moringa, sweet potato leaves, or spinach)
instructions: Leaf fritters are a common snack across the Indian Ocean world
Seychelles: moringa leaves (the drumstick tree) are native and used
The leaves dipped in a spiced chickpea batter
Fried until crispy
The Indian-influenced chickpea batter reflects the Seychellois Indian community
snacks.description: Seychellois leaf fritters -- moringa or sweet potato leaves dipped in spiced chickpea batter (Indian-influenced: the besan batter) and fried crispy. Moringa is native to the islands. Quick street snack.

snacks.name: Coconut Nougat
instructions: Coconut nougat is the Seychellois sweet -- made from the abundant local coconut
Grated coconut cooked with brown sugar until thick and caramelized
Set into bars or dropped onto paper to set
Sold at local markets -- a traditional confection
snacks.description: Seychellois coconut candy -- fresh grated coconut cooked with brown sugar until caramelized, set into bars. Made from the abundant island coconut. Sold at local markets.

snacks.name: Samoossa (Indian-Seychellois Samosa)
ingredients: Filling: spiced meat or vegetables (potato, peas)
instructions: Samoosa is the Seychellois version of the Indian samosa
The Indian community brought samosas to Seychelles
Adapted over generations to the Seychellois pantry
The triangular fried pastry is the same
Fillings adapted: local vegetables, local spice blends
snacks.description: Seychellois Indian-influenced samosa -- triangular fried pastry filled with spiced meat or vegetables. The Indian community brought samosas to Seychelles; they were adapted over generations to local spices and vegetables.

desserts.name: Ladob (Sweet)
instructions: Cook plantains in coconut milk with sugar and vanilla
Simmer until thick and syrupy
Grate nutmeg on top

desserts.name: Gato Banane (Banana Fritters)
instructions: Banana fritters are eaten throughout the tropical world
Seychelles: bananas grow on every island
The overripe bananas are mashed into a batter
Fried until golden -- crispy outside, banana-sweet inside
desserts.description: Seychellois banana fritters -- overripe bananas mashed into a batter with flour and egg, fried until golden and crispy. Bananas grow on every Seychellois island.

desserts.name: Gato Patate (Sweet Potato Cake)
instructions: Sweet potato cake cooked in coconut milk
A simple, naturally sweet cake from island sweet potato
The coconut milk and warm spices are the Seychellois flavors
desserts.description: Seychellois sweet potato cake -- cooked sweet potato mashed with coconut milk, sugar, and warm spices, baked until set. Island sweet potato, local coconut milk. Simple and naturally sweet.

drinks.name: Dite Citronelle (Lemongrass Tea)
instructions: Boil lemongrass in water 10 min
Strain, sweeten
Serve hot or cold

drinks.name: Calou (Palm Wine)
instructions: Collect sap from coconut palm
Drink fresh same day

drinks.name: Coco Fanny (Coconut Liqueur)
instructions: Coco Fanny is the Seychellois coconut cream liqueur
Made from local coconut with rum or locally-distilled spirit
Served cold over ice
The tropical coconut liqueur of the Seychelles
drinks.description: Seychellois coconut cream liqueur -- local coconut water and cream with rum and vanilla. The tropical island spirit of the Seychelles.
